problem: VLMs and VLAs in embodied decision making suffer from a perceptual bottleneck (object hallucination, omission, wrong attribute binding, miscounting) because they cannot separate task-relevant objects from distractors; one-step focus methods fail in cluttered scenes since they lack deep scene understanding.
motivation: Accurate focus on critical objects while suppressing clutter should break the bottleneck for both deliberate VLM planners and reactive VLA executors. Single-shot focus shows systematic mis-grounding and attention shifts, so progressive, scene-aware exploration is needed, and VLAs need a fast distilled version of it.
key_idea: Let the VLM generate a coarse-to-fine focus plan (scene-graph reasoning, then agentic zoom/search verification) that yields a focus mask dimming and blurring the background, and distill this into a lightweight slot-attention adapter for VLAs.
insight: Both stages matter: the ablations (Direct Focus, coarse-only, scene-graph-as-text) each recover only a fraction of the full gain, e.g. Qwen2.5-VL-7B Base 44.0 full vs 34.0 Direct Focus vs 37.3 coarse-only vs 30.7 text-graph. Raw scene-graph text adds noise, and thinking models do not fix perception (gemini thinking 70.0 vs Ours 74.7). Stress tests show fine-stage exploration recovers dropped graph nodes (RR >96%).
method: Coarse graph reasoning: OvSGTR builds a scene graph (objects with <ref>/<box>, relations <pred>) given as text; the VLM reasons over it to pick task-relevant sub-scenes, treating the VLM as source of truth.

Fine verification/exploration: the VLM zooms into each sub-scene with a limited field of view and agentically confirms, does a semantic zoom on ambiguity, or a local spatial search if the target is missing, producing verified candidate set C.
Focus modulation: candidate boxes are rasterized into a binary score map s; background is luminance-dimmed (floor beta) and Gaussian-blurred, giving a modulated image prompt.
SceneDiver adapter: placed after the VLA projector; task-guided Slot Attention (task-conditioned slot init, T=5 iterations, 256-d slots) extracts object-centric slots.
Scene-aware MaskNet: coarse slot relevance scores from semantics, slot mass and task context, plus a fine patch residual with alpha initialized near 0, giving a patch mask.
Distillation: Hungarian matching of slots to scene-graph objects with a Structure Loss and a Mask Loss; entropy-based gating bypasses masking under uncertainty.

setting.backbone: VLM branch: Qwen2.5-VL-7B/32B-AWQ, InternVL2.5-8B, gpt-4o-mini, gemini-2.5-flash, doubao-seed-1.6-flash (frozen, training-free), with OvSGTR scene graph generator (trained on synthetic simulator data); VLA branch: OpenVLA-OFT + adapter (fine-tuned)
setting.training_data: VLM branch: none (training-free) apart from OvSGTR trained on simulator-synthesized scene-graph data; VLA adapter trained on the interference-free LIBERO data (all four suites jointly)
setting.observation: monocular RGB images (current and target state images for manipulation)
setting.action_space: navigation: high-level discrete actions in EmbodiedBench (AI2-THOR); manipulation: discrete pick up/insert/reorient/put down; VLA: continuous low-level control of OpenVLA-OFT
setting.privileged: none at test time (scene graph predicted by OvSGTR)

numbers_note: No standard VLN benchmark; results are on custom/modified EmbodiedBench navigation, MuJoCo assembly and LIBERO-plus. Only representative cells listed; full tables have 12 columns per backbone.
results: On the harder room-navigation benchmark, SceneDiver beats the base model, SoM, Multi-Res, VCD and thinking variants across six VLMs (e.g. gemini-2.5-flash 74.7 vs 68.0 base and 70.0 for the best baselines; Qwen2.5-VL-7B 44.0 vs 32.7). It improves manipulation SR by 5-14 points and LIBERO-plus by 0.4-9.6 points over OpenVLA-OFT with 2.64% latency overhead.
limitations: Depends on a domain-specific scene graph generator trained on simulator data; extremely dynamic scenes not handled
Multi-stage VLM planning is computationally heavy (hence the adapter); evaluation limited to simulation with custom-modified benchmarks and small (30-scene) sets
Adapter gains on simple suites are small (e.g. under 1 point on Object)
